evidence.details: Target GitHub Actions workflow file requiring caching for pip/apt, trigger path filtering, and parallel job splitting to optimize median runtime (58s over 44 runs).

factual_findings: The workflow file .github/workflows/auto-merge-gate.yml currently records a median runtime of 58 seconds across 44 runs.
The current workflow configuration in .github/workflows/auto-merge-gate.yml does not cache pip or apt package dependencies across pipeline runs.
Triggers in .github/workflows/auto-merge-gate.yml run on all changes without paths filtering, executing test suites even when non-code files change.
Independent test steps in .github/workflows/auto-merge-gate.yml are currently executed sequentially in a single job rather than running concurrently across parallel jobs.
hypotheses: Integrating actions/cache (or setup-python built-in cache) for pip and apt dependencies in .github/workflows/auto-merge-gate.yml will eliminate repeated package downloads.
Adding paths filtering to workflow triggers in .github/workflows/auto-merge-gate.yml will skip workflow execution entirely for changes outside critical source paths.
Splitting sequential independent test tasks into parallel jobs in .github/workflows/auto-merge-gate.yml will decrease total wall-clock duration below the 58s median.
result.recommendation: Update .github/workflows/auto-merge-gate.yml to include path filters for pull_request/push triggers, configure caching for pip and apt dependencies using actions/cache, and decompose the workflow job into parallel execution jobs.
